context: Kshemaraja was the foremost disciple of Abhinavagupta and a prolific commentator. He wrote commentaries on the Shiva Sutras and the Spanda Karikas, as well as on major Shaiva tantras, and composed the Pratyabhijna Hridayam, a concise introduction to the philosophy of recognition. His works did much to transmit Kashmir Shaiva ideas in accessible form.
coreIdeas: Consciousness, entirely free, is the cause of the universe
The universe unfolds within consciousness as on a screen that is consciousness itself
The individual is universal consciousness in contracted form
Liberation is recognising one's own nature as Shiva, a recognition possible in the midst of ordinary experience
Shiva's five acts: creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment and grace
otherWorks: Shiva Sutra Vimarshini (commentary on the Shiva Sutras)
Commentaries on the Netra Tantra and Svacchanda Tantra
